metadata.notes: DeepSeek Harness creates a durable v3 session at TUI launch. The DSH adapter can show it as ready and bind its PID through session.lock.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

The load-bearing signals are a session row in `ready` within 1 second of launch and a PID bound within the same budget. DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 explicitly supports a fresh interactive session through `dsh --profile tui`. A launch-only probe on this host created `session.v3.jsonl.zstd` before any prompt. Its first durable record was a version-3 `session` header with the exact launch cwd. The same session directory contained `session.lock`. No model request was sent by that probe.

The daemon has two paths that can satisfy the birth signal. The DSH `FilesUnderRoot` source watches `~/.dsh/sessions`, accepts the highest `session.vN.jsonl.zstd` generation, and maps the session directory UUID. New daemon sessions start in `ready`. Independently, the generic process scanner uses the DSH `CommandPattern` with `pgrep -f`. A live launch showed the real command line as `node /Users/ingo/.nvm/versions/node/v22.18.0/bin/dsh --profile tui ...`, which matches the adapter regex `(^|/)dsh(\s|$)`. The scanner runs immediately and then at a 1-second default interval, and it creates a `proc-<PID>` ready pre-session when the transcript-backed session has not won the race.

PID binding is observable for either birth route. A pre-session carries its PID in `proc-<PID>`, and `PIDManager.TryDiscoverPID` binds it directly. For the real UUID session, `dsh.DiscoverPID` asks which process owns the sibling `session.lock`. The installed DSH JSONL persistence implementation documents and implements a POSIX `flock` on that file for the life of the write handle. The adapter therefore has a concrete live-process binding source.

The nudge recipe also exercises the real transcript path. A measured DSH v3 transcript contains `turn/start`, assistant messages with model `qwen/qwen3.5-9b` and non-zero usage, and terminal `turn/end {kind:completed}`. The DSH parser maps those records to `turn_start`, `assistant_message`, and `turn_done`, which produces the expected ready-to-working-to-ready arc. The interactive driver implements `send`, `wait_turn`, and `sleep`, and its temporary patch fixes the model to `qwen/qwen3.5-9b`. The 5-second trailing sleep matches the sibling session-start recipes and gives the daemon time to observe the final ready state.
caveats: Vacuous-pass check: the two timing phases can pass through the generic proc-<PID> pre-session even if the DSH file watcher or parser is broken. The recipe exercises the real compressed transcript and its ready-to-working-to-ready arc, but this session-start spec follows the fleet convention and leaves transcript-level arc assertions to basic-turn.
The 1-second acceptance budget depends on the daemon process scanner keeping its current 1-second default interval and on host load not delaying process or filesystem observation past the budget.
The daemon=full verdict is provisional until a recording measures birth and PID event timing. The source and launch probe prove the inputs exist, but this assessment did not run irrlichd.

The local model setting is load-bearing for the nudge turn: LM Studio must expose qwen/qwen3.5-9b at http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1. Otherwise the timing-only birth phases could pass while the transcript turn fails.

sources.note: Declares the FilesUnderRoot transcript source, CommandPattern process matcher, and PIDForSession binding for DeepSeek Harness.
Accepts the highest session.vN.jsonl.zstd generation under a session-UUID directory and defines the dsh command-line regex.
Maps v3 session, turn/start, assistant/message usage, and turn/end records into daemon lifecycle and metric signals.
Binds the real session PID through the sibling session.lock writer.
Runs an immediate process scan and then uses the 1-second default interval; a matched process creates a proc-<PID> pre-session.
TryDiscoverPID binds proc-<PID> sessions directly and uses the adapter PID discoverer for transcript-backed sessions.
Official installed package reference states that create takes write ownership, the JSONL backend writes one compressed log per session, and the write handle owns live persistence.
Installed implementation documents and implements the session.lock flock held for the write handle lifetime.
Launch-only probe: the transcript materialized before any prompt with a v3 session header and exact launch cwd; the sibling session.lock also existed.
Measured complete turn contains turn/start, qwen/qwen3.5-9b assistant usage with non-zero tokens, and turn/end completed.
Sibling recipe establishes the send, wait_turn, and 5-second settle sequence and the two-phase session-start scope.
Declares and implements send, wait_turn, and sleep, applies the fixed LM Studio model through a temporary patch, and fails when the durable transcript cannot be read.

preconditions: dsh 0.1.5-rc.2 or newer is on PATH and the community tui profile is installed under the active DSH home
LM Studio is serving qwen/qwen3.5-9b through http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1
irrlichd is recording with DeepSeek Harness transcript permission granted and uses the default 1-second process-scan interval
setup: Create an empty cwd under the recording staging directory
Let the driver apply the LM Studio endpoint and model through its per-run temporary patch

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: events.jsonl shows a session in ready within 1000 ms of agent launch
events.jsonl shows pid_discovered for that session within 1000 ms of agent launch
the real DSH UUID session completes one ready to working to ready turn
the nudge turn has no tool calls and ends in ready
the recording reports model qwen/qwen3.5-9b and non-zero tokens
